question: After the no-op pacing defect is fixed, should outbound recovery keep ambiguous rows pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available instead of moving them to failed?
rationale: Tests can prove either behavior, but the choice affects upgrade behavior and operator expectations: pending preserves future recoverability, while failed gives a clearer terminal state until the full delivery ledger exists.

options.title: Accept Recoverable Pending After Repair
options.body: Fix the pacing bug, then merge if maintainers want no-adapter ambiguous rows to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation or the broader ledger ships.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep current main's terminal failed behavior until the full delivery-state design is ready.

options.title: Require Operator Surface First
options.body: Ask for a doctor, UI, or API surfacing path before changing ambiguous rows to stay pending longer.

recommendation.title: Accept Recoverable Pending After Repair
recommendation.body: Fix the pacing bug, then merge if maintainers want no-adapter ambiguous rows to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation or the broader ledger ships.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses core queue semantics, message delivery behavior, and recent recovery merge ownership for the same files.
